dedupe_keys.name: eia 930 hourly electric grid monitor hourly demand forecast generation and interchange by us balancing authority

description: The Hourly Electric Grid Monitor publishes data collected on Form EIA-930, the Hourly and Daily Balancing Authority Operations Report, run by the U.S. Energy Information Administration. For each balancing authority, electricity region and the lower 48 states it gives hourly demand, day-ahead demand forecast, net generation, net generation by fuel type and by sub-balancing-authority region, and total and pairwise interchange between balancing authorities, with daily to yearly summaries including the peak demand hour. The respondents list read on the day has 68 active balancing authorities, 12 retired ones and 17 electricity regions. EIA API v2 serves the series hourly and in local time from January 2019, with the latest hour on 27 September 2026 when read. Coverage is the US grid by balancing authority. The data are accessible through the dashboard and the EIA API at no cost; as US government works they are in the public domain, and EIA asks users to acknowledge the source. Caveats: values are reported by the balancing authorities themselves and can be revised, and the API series read here start in 2019. Simulation uses are hourly demand and interchange inputs for grid models, and analysis of stress events such as heat waves and winter storms. Related records: data-open-grid-emissions and data-pudl process EIA electricity data.
